report
At Aurobindo Pharma Limited, we are pleased to present our Integrated Annual Report 
for FY26, offering a comprehensive overview of our performance, strategic priorities, 
governance practices and long-term value creation journey. 
Our integrated reporting 
approach provides stakeholders 
with a balanced and connected 
view of our financial and non-
financial performance, including 
manufacturing excellence, product 
development, sustainability, 
people practices and stakeholder 
engagement. It also outlines 
how we are building capabilities 
across complex and differentiated 
pharmaceutical segments while 
scaling responsibly across 
global markets.
This report is organised through 
the six capitals framework, namely 
Financial, Manufacturing, Intellectual, 
Human, Social and Relationship, 
and Natural Capital. It provides 
stakeholders with a balanced view 
of how we use, strengthen and 
protect these capitals to create 
sustained value.
REPORTING PERIOD
The report covers the financial year 
from April 1, 2025 to March 31, 2026, 
and includes material developments 
up to the date of approval by the 
Board of Directors on May 21, 2026.
REPORTING FRAMEWORKS 
AND PRINCIPLES
This report has been prepared in 
alignment with the principles of 
Integrated Reporting Framework 
as per International Integrated 
Reporting Council (IIRC), Global 
Reporting Initiative (GRI) and 
relevant sections of EU Corporate 
Sustainability Reporting Directive 
(CSRD). Relevant disclosures have 
also been aligned with applicable 
statutory requirements, including 
the Companies Act, 2013, SEBI 
(Listing Obligations and Disclosure 
Requirements) Regulations 
and Business Responsibility 
and Sustainability Reporting 
(BRSR) requirements.
The reporting process involves 
cross-functional participation across 
businesses, manufacturing sites and corporate functions to ensure a 
holistic and transparent representation 
of our operations, risks, opportunities 
and long-term priorities.
SCOPE AND BOUNDARY
The report covers Aurobindo Pharma 
Limited’s standalone and consolidated 
operations, including manufacturing 
facilities, research and development 
centres, commercial operations and 
corporate functions across geographies, 
unless stated otherwise. Sustainability-
related disclosures primarily cover 
manufacturing units, R&D centres and 
corporate offices across geographies 
based on operational relevance and 
data availability.
ASSURANCE AND DATA 
RELIABILITY
Financial information presented 
in this report is based on audited 
financial statements. Non-financial 
and sustainability-related information 
is compiled through internal 
reporting systems, functional 
reviews and management validation. 
The non-financial information has 
been assured by a third party with 
reasonable assurance in accordance 
with SEBI’s Business Responsibility 
and Sustainability Report (BRSR) 
requirements. Where applicable, 
disclosures are reviewed in line with 
statutory requirements and internal 
controls to ensure consistency, 
accuracy and reliability.

FORWARD-LOOKING 
STATEMENTS
Certain statements in this report may 
contain forward-looking perspectives 
relating to the Company’s future

and operating performance. Actual

to changes in market conditions, 
regulatory developments, economic 
factors and other external variables.

Strength today, Momentum ahead.
&Purpose
Progress.
Decades of For four decades, Aurobindo Pharma has 
remained guided by a clear purpose: to 
make high-quality medicines affordable 
and accessible to patients across 
the world. What began with a single 
manufacturing unit has grown into a 
large, integrated global pharmaceutical 
platform, built on scale, science, 
reliability and trust.
The journey has been one of steady 
progress. We expanded from APIs 
to formulations, from oral solids to 
injectables, from generics to complex 
products and biosimilars, strengthening 
our relevance across regulated 
and growth markets. Each step has 
enhanced our ability to serve evolving 
healthcare needs while building a more 
resilient, future-ready business.
Today, our strength rests on deep 
manufacturing capabilities, backward 
integration, a broad product portfolio, 
disciplined R&D and a presence across 
150+ countries. We are the largest 
generic pharma company in the US by prescriptions dispensed, rank among 
the top 10 generic companies in eight 
European countries and are the third-
largest listed Indian pharma company by 
revenue from operations.
Purpose, for us, extends beyond 
products and markets. It reflects how 
we operate, conserve resources, engage 
with communities and create value 
responsibly. Our sustainability journey 
continues to focus on cleaner operations, 
water stewardship, waste management, 
responsible sourcing and meaningful 
social impact, aligned with our ambition 
to grow responsibly and deliver 
lasting value.As we enter the next chapter, our 
momentum is being shaped by 
clear strategic priorities: expanding 
manufacturing capacity, strengthening 
supply chain resilience, advancing 
biosimilars and biologics, growing in 
high-potential markets and building 
differentiated portfolios across 
specialty, respiratory, peptides and 
complex injectables.4 Decades of Purpose & Progress 
captures both the foundation we have 
built and the future we are preparing 
for. It reflects our commitment to 
healthier lives, our confidence in 
disciplined execution and our belief that 
enduring value is created by serving 
patients, strengthening capabilities and 
moving forward with conviction.

 Integrated Annual Report 2025-26CORPORATE OVERVIEW Statutory Reports Financial Statements 20Building depth across  
complex therapies
We continue to strengthen our presence across complex and specialty 
therapeutic areas through differentiated formulations, advanced delivery 
platforms and biosimilars, focused on improving treatment outcomes, 
accessibility and patient convenience worldwide.
CURATEQ BIOLOGICS  - BUILDING A GLOBAL BIOSIMILARS 
PORTFOLIO 
CuraTeQ Biologics, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Aurobindo Pharma, is 
developing a portfolio of biosimilars aimed at widening patient access to 
complex, high-cost biologic therapies. Its approach combines in-house 
development and manufacturing capability with a commercialisation 
footprint spanning the EU and emerging markets, complemented by 
selective entry into the US, with a longer-term aim of establishing itself 
as a significant biosimilars player by 2030. During FY26, CuraTeQ secured 
biosimilar approvals across multiple regulated markets, including 
Europe, the UK and Canada.
Biosimilars
REGULATORY APPROVALS
  Dazublys (trastuzumab biosimilar referencing Herceptin) received a positive CHMP opinion from the European 
Medicines Agency in April 2025, followed by European Commission marketing authorisation in July 2025, for 
the treatment of HER2-positive breast and gastric cancers — CuraTeQ's first EU-approved oncology biosimilar. 
Dazublys was also approved by Medicines and Healthcare Products Regulatory Agency in August 2025 and is 
currently under review with Health Canada
  Dyrupeg (pegfilgrastim biosimilar referencing Neulasta) received marketing authorisation by European 
Commission Apr 2025, Medicines and Healthcare Products in June 2025, and Health Canada in January 2026

FY26 marks an important milestone 
in the journey of Aurobindo

Over the last forty years, we

API manufacturer into one of the 
world's leading pharmaceutical 
companies, serving patients 
across more than 150 countries. 
This journey has been defined 
by a commitment to quality, 
affordability, operational excellence 
and the belief that sustainable 
success is built through discipline, 
resilience and long-term thinking.
The global business environment 
remained dynamic during the 
year. While inflationary pressures 
moderated and supply chains 
continued to stabilise, geopolitical 
developments, evolving trade 
dynamics and regulatory 
complexities continued to shape 
the operating landscape. At the 
same time, the pharmaceutical 
industry is undergoing a structural 
transformation, with increasing 
emphasis on complex generics, 
specialty products, injectables 
and biologics. Companies that 
can successfully combine scale, 
innovation, compliance and supply 
chain resilience are increasingly 
emerging as long-term winners.Against this backdrop, Aurobindo 
Pharma delivered another year of 
resilient performance. Revenue 
from operations reached ` 33,653 
crore and EBITDA stood at ` 6,856 
crore, reflecting the strength of 
our diversified business model, 
broad geographic presence and 
disciplined execution. More 
importantly, the quality of growth 
continued to improve, supported 
by portfolio diversification, 
operational efficiencies and 
sustained momentum across 
key businesses.

of FY26 was the exceptional 
performance of our European 
business, which crossed the 
significant milestone of €1 
billion in annual revenues. This 
achievement reflects years of

supply capabilities and a steadily 
expanding product portfolio.

Biosimilars are becoming a larger commercial 
opportunity as healthcare systems seek more 
affordable biologic therapies. Patent expiries across 
high-value biologics, especially in oncology and 
immunology, are expected to create opportunities 
for companies with strong clinical, regulatory and 
manufacturing capabilities. While 118 biologics 
are expected to lose patent protection in the 
US during 2025-2034, only 12 had biosimilars 
in development as of June 2024, highlighting a 
sizeable biosimilar void.Our response
Through CuraTeQ Biologics, we are 
building a focused biosimilars platform 
across oncology and immunology, with 
a portfolio of 14 products. Two products 
have successfully completed Phase 3 
trials and two are currently in Phase 3. We 
initiated supplies for multiple biosimilars 
in the UK and select European markets, 
entered into a licensing agreement for 
distributing two EMA-approved biosimilars 
in select EU territories and are adding bulk 
manufacturing and filling capacities to 
support future launches.

to face concentration risks, geopolitical 
uncertainty, cost volatility and periodic drug 
shortages. This has increased the importance of 
backward integration, localised manufacturing 
and flexible supply networks, particularly for 
companies serving regulated markets such as 
the US and Europe.Our response
We are strengthening global manufacturing 
and supply chain resilience through integrated 
capacities and backward integration. In 
FY26, we incurred capex investments of

production internally. Our Pen-G facility was 
commercialised and stabilised, with annualised 
production expected to exceed 10,000 MT 
based on current operating levels. We also

and frameworks. We maintain all necessary EHSS-related statutory permits across our manufacturing facilities,

evolving regulatory landscape.International Collaborations

Prioritising our 
MATERIAL ISSUES FOR FY26MATERIALITY ASSESSMENTmost material issues 
We recognise the critical role of materiality assessment in identifying and 
prioritising the issues that matter most to our operations and stakeholders. 
We adopt a double materiality framework, enabling us to evaluate both our 
impact on the environment and society as well as the financial implications 
of sustainability-related risks and opportunities. This integrated approach 
helps us address stakeholder expectations and navigate emerging risks 
and opportunities.
We undertook a comprehensive 
double materiality assessment 
in FY25, aligned with the 
requirements of the Corporate 
Sustainability Reporting 
Directive (CSRD). The assessment 
enabled the identification of key 
sustainability topics that are 
most crucial to our business and stakeholders. The process began 
with identifying a universe of 
issues relevant to APL’s operations. 
These were determined through 
an integrated review of global 
frameworks and standards, ESG 
rating methodologies, emerging 
megatrends, existing material 
topics, and peer benchmarking.The assessment involved two key 
dimensions- Impact Materiality 
and Financial Materiality. 
The materiality approach and 
outcomes are monitored by core 
members and overseen by the ESG 
Committee and will be reviewed 
annually to maintain relevance 
and accuracy.APPROACH TO DOUBLE MATERIALITY

ANTIMICROBIAL 
RESISTANCE
Stakeholders 
impacted
Whether Risk or Opportunity
Risk
Impact and its description
Negative impact
Improper management of antibiotic waste during 
manufacturing can release active pharmaceutical 
ingredients (APIs) into the environment, 
contaminating aquatic ecosystems with trace 
drug residues. This disrupts aquatic life, threatens 
biodiversity, and fuels antimicrobial resistance 
(AMR), a growing global public health and 
environmental crisis. Effective and scalable 
solutions to manage this risk are still being sought.
Description of risk
-Description of opportunity
-
Management approach
Member of the ‘AMR Industry alliance since 
2019,’ which is driving antimicrobial resistance 
progress via common objectives and commitment 
to increase access to high-quality antimicrobial 
products, encourage responsible usage, and 
reduce environmental concerns. APL has been 
participating in the Access to Medicine (AMR 
Benchmark) Survey since 2018.WASTE MANAGEMENT AND

impacted

Description of risk
 Irresponsible waste management and inefficient

Navigating risks  RISK MANAGEMENTand uncertainties
We operate within a highly regulated pharmaceutical industry, making 
risk management crucial for maintaining the safety, quality, and efficacy 
of our products. With a complex and widespread global footprint and 
manufacturing facilities, our business is exposed to a diverse range of 
risks. We adopt a structured approach to risk management, underpinned by 
strong governance and robust systems, ensuring long-term value creation.
ENTERPRISE RISK 
MANAGEMENT (ERM) 
FRAMEWORK
Our ERM framework is designed 
to effectively identify and mitigate 
key business risks. Aligned 
with the globally recognised 
COSO ERM Framework (2017), 
developed by the Treadway 
Commission, our approach 
integrates risk management 
into strategic planning and 
operations. The framework 
focuses on minimising the 
adverse impact of risks and 
capitalising on emerging opportunities, strengthening 
organisational resilience and 
capability to navigate uncertainties. 
RISK GOVERNANCE 
STRUCTURE
We have established a 
comprehensive risk governance 
structure, which ensures 
accountability, oversight, and 
alignment with business priorities. 
The risk management function is 
led by the Risk Management Head 
and supported by Business and 
Functional Heads. The risk function 
reports to the Risk Management Committee (RMC), with the Board 
of Directors as the ultimate 
governing body.  
The RMC, chaired by Mr. Girish 
Paman Vanvari, with Mr. Santanu 
Mukherjee and Dr. Madan Mohan 
Reddy as members, plays a pivotal 
role in overseeing risk-related 
matters. The committee has 
established a risk management 
policy to address strategic, 
business, and operational risks.
Risk management processes are 
regularly reviewed by the Board 
of Directors. Our ERM framework highlights the following risk categories:The ultimate governing 
body that provides 
strategic direction and 
ensures oversight of risk 
management activities
RMC, comprising senior 
executives and risk management 
experts, sets policies, reviews 
risk assessments, and monitors 
risk mitigation efforts
Oversees implementation 
of the ERM framework and 
coordinates with business and 
functional heads to identify, 
assess, and address risks 
Identifies and manages risks 
within their respective areas of 
responsibility, embedding the 
risk considerations into business 
processes and decisionsBoard
Business Unit / 
Functional HeadsRisk Management 
TeamRisk Management 
Committee
  Risk categories Ownership
Strategic risks
Risks on markets, products, resources, business growth & revenue model, investment, 
etc., which may impact business objectivesTop Management
Operational risk 
Risks relating to business operations like production capacity, quality assurance, 
customer demand, availability of materials, human safety, etc., which can 
impact businessOperations Team
Project risk
Risks pertaining to projects like commissioning delays and budget overruns that can 
impact business and lead to financial lossesFunctional Heads
Compliance risks
Risks pertaining to regulatory and statutory compliance, which can impact reputation 
and business operationsFunctional Heads
Financial risks
Risks pertaining to the efficient utilisation of financial resources, such as currency 
fluctuations, credit risks, and liquidity risks, which can impact revenue, profitability, 
and liquidity.Chief Financial 
Officer (CFO)
Information Technology (IT) risks
Risks pertaining to IT, like technology obsolescence, cyber-attacks, breach of security, 
data loss, etc., which can impact business operations and reputationChief Information 
Officer (CIO)

The US and Europe constitute our

Impact

sales volumes

strategic acquisitions 
  Driving cost competitiveness and enhancing 
manufacturing capabilities 
  Timely launch of new products 
  Micro-level inventory planning to ensure 
uninterrupted availability of materials

Risk description and impact on value 
We operate across key global markets 
that are subject to pricing regulations and 
cost-containment measures, particularly 
in the US, where government initiatives 
aimed at reducing drug prices continue 
to intensify pricing pressures. These 
challenges are further compounded by 
the consolidation of drug wholesalers, 
retail chains, and group purchasing 
organisations, strengthening their 
bargaining power.
In domestic markets, pricing dynamics 
are influenced by global trends in 
the availability and cost of imported 
raw materials and APIs. Additionally, 
industry-wide price controls, competitive 
discounting, and the need to maintain 
price parity further add to the pressure 
on realisations.
Impact
Evolving pricing regulations and 
sustained pricing pressures may limit the 
financial benefits from market expansion 
and new product launches. Increased 
discounting to retain market share can 
reduce margins, adversely impacting 
revenues and profitability.S5
Risk mitigation 
 We address pricing pressures by 
launching value-added products and 
expanding into complex segments, 
such as injectables, ophthalmology, and 
oncology. We are also focusing on growth 
markets where pricing pressures are 
lower, while ensuring stable supplies and 
a broader product portfolio
 Our focus on quality and compliance 
helps minimise the risk of 
commoditisation. A well-diversified 
portfolio in key markets such as the 
US further supports resilience against 
pricing pressures. Our R&D teams 
drive cost efficiency through process 
innovation, automation, and continuous 
improvement in manufacturing practices
 We actively manage pricing challenges 
by optimising cost structures, reducing 
cost of goods sold (COGS), improving 
efficiencies, scaling volumes, and 
strengthening supply chain
 Our supply chain management (SCM) 
team focuses on strategic sourcing and 
vendor negotiations to mitigate raw 
material cost volatility and ensure timely 
service to customers in key markets
 Backward integration enhances our ability 
to manufacture high-quality products 
at competitive costs by redefining the 
production process and leveraging 
R&D capabilities

We operate across a wide range of markets,

We also have a presence in the anti-retroviral

Given the evolving geopolitical landscape, 
including ongoing conflicts in regions such as 
the Middle East, we face potential disruptions in 
supply chains. These may arise from extended 
transit times, increased freight costs due to 
fluctuations in crude oil prices, and higher 
insurance costs. Economic or political instability, 
policy changes, and evolving regulatory 
frameworks across markets may further impact 
our operations.
Impact
Geopolitical uncertainties and economic 
instability may disrupt supply chains, delay 
regulatory approvals, and affect participation 
in global tenders. These can impact revenue, 
increase compliance costs, and create barriers to 
market access.Risk mitigation 
 We continue to expand our presence through 
business and R&D acquisitions across the 
Developed Countries  while penetrating high-
potential markets, such as Japan, Brazil, Africa, 
Canada, the Middle East, and select European 
regions including Poland, the Czech Republic, the 
Netherlands, Spain, and Belgium
 We are enhancing presence in complex, niche, 
and specialty segments, such as oral solids,

peptide-based products. 58% of our FY26 R&D 
spending was in these areas
 In regions such as Africa, the Middle East, and 
Russia, we adopt a calibrated market approach 
by participating in government tenders and 
strengthening our distributor network. This helps

economic, and regulatory factors, including local 
manufacturing mandates, import restrictions, and 
logistics constraints
 We follow prudent credit practices, including 
securing payments through advance payment

in high-risk countries

Formulation 
Dependency on 
Bulk DrugsStrategy at risk Process owner
Operations  
Head - APIS1 S2 S4
Risk description and impact on value 
In the pharmaceutical value chain, bulk drug 
manufacturing units produce APIs, which 
are essential building blocks for finished 
formulations. Formulation facilities rely on 
a consistent and timely supply of APIs to 
manufacture final dosage forms such as 
tablets, capsules, and injectables. 
This interdependence creates a potential 
single point of vulnerability. Any disruption 
in bulk drug production, arising from 
regulatory actions, equipment failures, 
natural calamities, or raw material 
shortages, can impact the continuity of 
formulation operations.
Impact
A potential shutdown or disruption at 
bulk manufacturing facilities may impact 
formulation output, resulting in loss of 
revenue, reduced capacity utilisation, and 
disruption in customer supplies. Risk mitigation 
 As part of our de-risking strategy, we are developing 
alternate manufacturing facilities for select products 
to support future growth. We have also identified 
and approved 2–3 external API vendors across 
different geographies for all high-volume and critical 
molecules. The formulation (FDF) units procure 
intermediates directly from third parties to reduce 
dependency on APIs
 Our FDF units directly procure materials to 
balance supply chain risks while maintaining 
cost competitiveness. Our strong Regulatory 
Affairs and Quality Assurance (QA) teams ensure 
compliance across markets, supported by dedicated 
R&D capabilities and technological expertise in 
specialised formulations
 Our supply chain function focuses on vendor 
development and price assurance, while R&D 
explores innovative ways to optimise raw material 
consumption or identify suitable substitutes. We 
maintain a safety stock of 5–6 months and enter 
into forward contracts with key vendors to ensure 
supply continuity
 Our SCM team focuses on developing alternate 
sourcing options and investing in backward 
integration for critical raw materials. For most 
APIs, we have either alternate vendors or in-
house manufacturing capabilities to mitigate 
supply disruptions
 We have undertaken the following measures as part 
of vendor evaluation and monitoring: 
  Strict adherence to quality standards for materials 
and intermediates 
  Comprehensive contractual terms covering delays 
and supply disruptions 
  Continuous monitoring of vendors, especially those 
exposed to environmental or operational risks 
  Periodic and surprise audits at vendor sites to 
ensure compliance 
  Regular vendor qualification by the Corporate 
Quality Assurance (CQA) team, with immediate 
delisting in case of significant deviations

Head - APIS4
Risk description and impact on value 
In the pharmaceutical industry, APIs are 
manufactured at specialised facilities, where 
production for certain products is concentrated 
at a single site. This creates a critical dependency 
on individual manufacturing locations.
Any disruption at such facilities, arising from 
equipment failure, quality or contamination 
issues, regulatory non-compliance, or 
unforeseen events, can halt production. The 
absence of alternative manufacturing sites for 
certain key products increases this vulnerability.
Impact
Disruptions at a single manufacturing 
facility may lead to production delays and 
supply shortages.Risk mitigation 
 As part of our de-risking strategy, we are 
developing additional manufacturing facilities for 
critical product segments, such as cephalosporin, 
oncology, and penicillin, aligned with 
future growth
 We aim to maintain 2–3 approved Contract 
Manufacturing Organisations (CMOs) as backup 
suppliers for each critical API. Pre-approved 
technology transfer packages are in place to 
enable rapid activation within defined timelines
 We have identified 2–3 qualified suppliers for 
all key starting materials (KSM) and advanced 
intermediates. We have also secured long-term 
capacity through 3–4 year agreements with 
multiple CMOs, including assured volumes, 
technology transfer rights, and structured 
pricing mechanisms
 We are leveraging government initiatives such as 
the Production Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme and 
state-level incentives to support the development 
of additional API capacities, new API parks and 
brownfield expansions, accelerating multi-site 
manufacturing capabilities

Governance that   GOVERNANCEsustains progress
For a global pharmaceutical company, governance is a business-critical 
discipline. At Aurobindo Pharma, it shapes how decisions are made, how 
risks are reviewed, how compliance is monitored and how accountability is 
maintained across markets, operations and functions.
Our approach is anchored in 
clear Board oversight, defined 
policies, transparent reporting 
and a strong culture of ethical 
conduct. These elements help us 
operate with consistency across a 
complex regulatory environment, 
while protecting the interests of 
patients, employees, partners, 
shareholders and communities.CORPORATE GOVERNANCE 
AND BOARD OVERSIGHT
Our governance framework is 
designed to support responsible 
decision-making, regulatory 
compliance and effective oversight 
across the organisation. It 
provides the structure through 
which business priorities, risk 
management, statutory obligations and sustainability matters are 
reviewed and monitored.
The Board plays an active role in 
guiding governance standards and 
overseeing compliance. It engages 
periodically with the management 
and relevant stakeholders to 
review progress, assess emerging 
risks and guide corrective actions 
where required.To strengthen compliance 
monitoring, we have deployed 
a statutory compliance system 
across our operations. Quarterly 
declarations are submitted to 
the Compliance Officer, enabling 
structured review and timely 
follow-up. This mechanism 
supports consistent tracking 
of regulatory obligations 
across geographies and 
business functions.
Given the nature of our 
business, regulatory discipline 
is also embedded within 
product development and 
filing processes. Our scientists, 
analysts and regulatory teams 
work together to ensure that 
submissions are aligned with 
local requirements and that 
our products continue to 
meet applicable quality and 
safety expectations.BOARD DIVERSITY , 
COMPOSITION AND ESG 
OVERSIGHT
The Board brings together 
experience across healthcare, 
finance, manufacturing, academia 
and other relevant areas. This 
diversity of expertise supports 
balanced deliberation and 
enables informed oversight of 
strategic priorities, operational 
risks, compliance matters and 
sustainability performance.
As of March 31, 2026, Independent 
Directors comprised 44.4% of 
the Board and women members 
represented 11.11%.
The Board also provides oversight 
on ESG-related matters, including 
goal-setting, performance review, 
compliance with applicable 
standards and alignment with 
broader sustainability priorities. 
This helps ensure that ESG considerations are addressed 
through established governance 
structures rather than as 
standalone initiatives.
POLICY FRAMEWORKS
Policies form the basis for 
consistent conduct across 
the organisation. They define 
responsibilities, set behavioural 
expectations and provide 
guidance on key areas such as 
ethics, compliance, workplace 
conduct, safety, sustainability, 
responsible sourcing, human 
rights and stakeholder protection.
The Board periodically reviews 
and updates these policies to 
reflect regulatory changes, 
business needs and evolving 
governance expectations. This 
helps keep the policy framework 
relevant to the scale, geography 
and complexity of Aurobindo 
Pharma’s operations.

BUSINESS OVERVIEW
The United States remains our 
largest and most strategically 
significant market, supported by 
scale, portfolio breadth and a 
strong commercial infrastructure. 
Our business spans oral solids, 
injectables, OTC, specialty and oncology products, backed 
by diversified manufacturing 
capabilities and long-standing 
customer relationships.
We continue to strengthen the 
business through differentiated 
product development, strategic 
partnerships and investments across newer technologies 
such as MDI/DPI products, 
transdermals and derma 
foams. Alongside this, we are 
advancing digital and AI-led 
capabilities through initiatives 
such as SparkAI to enhance 
agility, productivity and data-led 
decision-making.
KEY BUSINESS DEVELOPMENTS, FY26
• US formulations business recorded revenue 
of USD 1,631 million as against USD 1,752 
million in FY25, impacted by lower transient 
sales supported by stable base business 
performance, and continued execution 
across oral solids, however injectables and 
OTC products
• APUSA entered into a definitive agreement 
to acquire Lannett Inc., an Indiana-based 
manufacturing company focused primarily on 
controlled substances, particularly in the ADHD 
segment. Subject to regulatory approvals, 
the acquisition is expected to close during 
FY27 and strengthen our US manufacturing 
footprint, deepen our presence in controlled substances and support expansion into 
differentiated dosage formats
• Acrotech received USFDA approval for Adquey® 
(difamilast) ointment 1% for the topical 
treatment of mild-to-moderate atopic dermatitis 
in adults and paediatric patients aged two 
years and above. The product is expected to be 
launched during the first half of FY27
• APUSA launched 34 products during the year, 
while Acrotech launched one oncology product 
and AuroHealth launched three products
• US injectable business witnessed improved 
performance supported by supply ramp-up and 
new launches
GROWTH DRIVERS
Volume-led Scale
Our volume-based strategy, global 
capacities and strong talent pool 
have helped create a sustainable 
engine for growth, reinforcing our 
position as a generic powerhouse 
in the US market.
Specialty Generics Pipeline
We have several specialty generics 
products in the pipeline across DPI/
MDI, transdermal and derma foam 
formats, which are expected to 
support meaningful growth over 
the medium term.
OTC Growth Momentum
Surging volumes in OTC products 
continue to strengthen our portfolio 
breadth and support growth across 
the US business.
Partnership-led Business 
Development
Our newly established business 
development team is actively pursuing partnership opportunities 
to bring a more differentiated 
portfolio of products to the market.
MANUFACTURING AND 
REGULATORY UPDATES
Aurologistics, a wholly-owned 
subsidiary of APUSA, commenced 
operations at a newly constructed 
warehouse facility at the East 
Windsor campus to support 
expanding OTC and injectable 
volumes and strengthen 
distribution-readiness.
At the Dayton, New Jersey facility, 
Aurolife completed regulatory 
filings for select products and 
progressed towards USFDA 
inspection-readiness. The Raleigh, 
North Carolina facility also 
continued progressing towards 
regulatory inspection during 
the year.OUTLOOK
We remain confident in the 
long-term outlook for our 
US business, supported 
by portfolio diversification, 
differentiated product 
development and 
global manufacturing 
infrastructure. Future 
growth is expected to 
be driven by specialty 
launches, strategic 
partnerships, injectable 
expansion and increasing 
contributions from newer 
technology platforms.
Our focus remains 
on strengthening the 
complex generics and 
specialty portfolio, scaling 
operational efficiencies and 
building a more diversified 
and future-ready US 
business platform.

During FY26, we continued 
strengthening the network 
through capacity enhancement,

ramp-up initiatives across 
formulations, dermatology,

and oral solid dosage facilities. 
Manufacturing, packing and

and expanded installed capacity to

annually. Commercial supplies

future scalability.

COST REDUCTION
Several initiatives were 
undertaken to reduce cycle

These included debottlenecking

automated handling systems. These 
measures improved operational 
productivity, reduced manual

supply responsiveness.
Yield improvement, energy

through process optimisation,

Our operational excellence agenda

improvement, capability building 
and scaling operational best 
practices across facilities.
During the year, several 
manufacturing excellence initiatives 
received external recognition 
through CII awards across energy

excellence practices.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS 
• Filed 25 ANDAs during the year, with more than 25% 
concentrated in complex and specialty therapeutic categories
• Received 40 ANDA approvals (including tentative approvals), 
reflecting strong regulatory execution capabilities
• Continued strengthening First-to-File (FTF) and Paragraph IV 
filing strategies
• Advanced development across complex generics, derma, nasal, 
inhalation, injectables and biosimilars, with a sharper focus on 
high-barrier products and specialty dosage forms
• Strengthened development discipline through Quality by Design 
frameworks and lifecycle management initiatives
• Continued improving development timelines through focused 
project governance and efficient execution
Eugia Pharma
Eugia Pharma is focused on developing differentiated specialty and 
complex injectable products across oncology and other critical therapeutic 
areas. Its R&D efforts are centred around high-barrier injectables, long-
acting depot formulations, GLP-1 agonists, liposomal and nanoparticle 
platforms, as well as advanced device-based delivery systems including 
auto-injectors and pen injectors.
KEY DEVELOPMENTS 
• Filed the generic version of Invega Sustenna, Paliperidone 
palmitate injectable suspension
• Continued progressing towards filing generic versions of Mounjaro 
and Zepbound on NCE-1 timelines
• Added two new injectable technology platforms: liposomal 
injectables and nanoparticle-engineered products
• Continued establishing advanced manufacturing capabilities for 
these platforms at the Genome Valley oncology facility
• Recorded 54 global filings across major markets, including 4 US 
ANDA filings
• Received 31 approvals across major markets and completed 
38 launches
• Key launches included Dasatinib, Icatibant, Pomalidomide, 
Nintedanib, Progesterone and Enzalutamide across 
key geographies
• Continued progressing GLP-1 agonist and device-based injectable 
pipeline capabilities
Apitoria Pharma
Apitoria Pharma specialises in developing NCE-1 products, novel processes and greener technologies, including 
biocatalysis, flow chemistry and solvent or reagent optimisation. Focused on delivering affordable, high-quality 
APIs, it continues to strengthen process development, lifecycle management, quality systems and differentiated 
chemistry capabilities.
KEY DEVELOPMENTS 
• Expanded focus on Oncology APIs, peptides and complex APIs across CNS, CVS and 
antidiabetic therapies
• Strengthened capabilities in NCE-1 molecules and high-barrier synthesis platforms
• Integrated biocatalysis, flow chemistry and homogenisation technologies into core R&D operations
• Advanced Analytical Quality by Design (AQbD)-driven method development and 
validation frameworks
• Developed 7+ novel polymorphs through high-end polymorph screening capabilities
• Continued improving process robustness, yield enhancement and impurity control across 
development programmes
• Advanced green chemistry principles to support safer and more sustainable process developmentPRUDENT R&D APPROACH

a strong understanding of community needs, aligned with our CSR Policy and the United Nations Sustainable 
Development Goals (SDGs).

ADVANCING SKILL 
DEVELOPMENT AND 
EMPLOYABILITY  
Through our network of 
Aurobindo Pharma Foundation 
Skill Development Centres across 
Andhra Pradesh and Telangana, 
we continue to enhance skill 
development and employability 
among rural youth. 
At Varisam village, Srikakulam 
district, Andhra Pradesh, 393 M.Sc. 
and M.Pharm graduates received 
advanced industry training, with 
78% successfully placed. In the 
Indrakaran village of Sangareddy 
district, Telangana, 552 trainees 
(including B.Pharm, D.Pharm, ITI, 
and diploma holders) completed 
training programmes, with 98% 
securing employment. 
In the Mulapeta village of Kakinada, 
Andhra Pradesh, the Prathibha 
Computer Training Centre trained 
695 rural unemployed youth 
in computer, coding, and soft 
skills. The Women’s Vocational 
Training Centre trained 529 
women in tailoring, 78% of whom 
have established independent 
businesses. At Gorantlapally 
village, Annamayya district, Andhra 
Pradesh, 114 youth and 71 women 
were trained in computer skills and 
tailoring, respectively. 
Further, we established a new Skill 
Development Centre at Andhra 
University, Visakhapatnam, to 
provide high-end training for 
underprivileged graduates in the 
pharma and healthcare sectors. We 
also supported a skill development 
programme by Reddy Seva Samithi 
Trust, providing computer and 
soft skills training to 180 young 
women in the Kadapa district, 
Andhra Pradesh.

FREE BREAKFAST MEALS 
PROGRAMME, KAKINADA 
In collaboration with the Hare 
Krishna Movement Charitable 
Foundation (HKMCF), we undertook 
a large-scale free breakfast meals 
programme powered by India’s first 
fully solar-powered HKMCF kitchen 
in Perumallapuram, Kakinada 
district, Andhra Pradesh, established 
by Aurobindo Pharma Foundation 
in 2022. This centralised, automated 
kitchen serves free hygienic 
breakfast meals to 6,000 students 
daily across 46 government schools 
in nearby villages. 
The programme supports children 
from fishing communities, where 
early morning livelihoods often 
result in students attending 
school on an empty stomach or 
dropping out. To address this, the 
programme provides nutritious, 
millet-based breakfasts to meet 
the nutritional requirements of 
students. Since its inception, 
32.86 lakh free meals have been 
served, enhancing child health & 
educational outcomes and reduced 
student dropout rates.

CASE STUDY
ADVANCING OUTREACH AT AUROBINDO 
ONCOLOGY BLOCK, HYDERABAD 
We continued our efforts to expand outreach at 
the Aurobindo Oncology Block in Hyderabad, 
established in 2023, delivering meaningful 
outcomes for patients. In FY26, the Aurobindo 
Oncology Block witnessed a footfall of 200 
outpatients per day and nearly 90 daily admissions. 
With 260 beds consistently occupied, both 
inpatient and outpatient services recorded a 20% 
increase. Day care chemotherapy services also 
expanded by 10%, with streamlined protocols 
enabling simpler cases to be managed at District 
Cancer Chemotherapy Centres under expert 
supervision, allowing the facility to focus on 
complex treatments.
A dedicated Adolescent and Young Adult (AYA) 
ward provides specialised care for this age 
group, offering access to advanced oncology 
treatments and medications at no cost. The Bone 
Marrow Transplant programme has expanded 
from 4 to 6 procedures per month, with 60 new 
transplants conducted and 124 follow-up cases 
managed. Through mobile screening camps conducted in collaboration with MNJ, 19,954 
individuals were screened for oral, breast, and 
cervical cancers. 
The Aurobindo Oncology Block has treated 1.6 
lakh patients across 7 states during the year, 
creating a lasting impact on people’s lives.SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE

SHORT-TERM HR STRATEGIES
Rapid hiring: 
We continue to follow an any-time recruitment 
approach to address attrition, constrained 
expansion and business-critical hiring needs. 
Greater emphasis is being placed on skill-based 
hiring and AI-enabled solutions to improve 
sourcing precision, bridge critical talent gaps 
and support timely onboarding.
Business continuity through core talent: 
The Career Enablement Programme helps 
retain key contributors and supports continuity 
across priority roles, reducing the risk of 
leadership or capability gaps.
Attrition risk buffering: 
The Talent Retention Policy supports proactive 
and responsive interventions for predicted 
and unpredicted attrition, helping minimise 
disruption and protect operational continuity.LONG-TERM HR STRATEGIES
Building leadership pipeline: 
Second Line Development continues to 
strengthen leadership depth and build 
resilience during transitions.
Scaling technical excellence: 
Training Within Industry, Job Instruction 
methodology continues to bridge shopfloor 
skill gaps. The Apitoria Capability Centre, 
Takshashila, was launched for the Hyderabad 
cluster, while a similar capability centre 
for the Vizag cluster is planned to support 
employee upskilling.
Strategic workforce design: 
We continue to focus on talent engagement, 
development and retention, while planning 
for superannuation-led vacancies and 
generational continuity. Talent consolidation 
also supports integration efficiency and helps 
build a future-fit workforce.

strengthened leadership support

Hiring efficiency and workforce-
readiness
During the year, our hiring 
strategy focused on localised 
talent harvesting hubs, including 
pharmacy colleges, polytechnics 
and ITIs. This helped create a more 
stable talent pipeline, improve 
long-term engagement and support 
attrition reduction. This was 
complemented by in-house training 
through the Skill Development

through government-sponsored

framework. This evaluates 
candidates on technical capability, 
behavioural traits, cultural 
alignment and long-term potential, 
helping improve quality of hire and 
career sustainability.
Our AI- and ML-enabled 
recruitment platform continued 
to improve sourcing effectiveness 
by matching candidate profiles 
with role requirements, enhancing 
speed, precision and diversity in 
talent acquisition.

DIVERSITY , EQUITY AND INCLUSION
Diversity, equity and inclusion remains integral to our organisational culture. We provide equal opportunities to 
all employees, regardless of age, gender identity, religion, caste, nationality, race or ethnicity. Our recruitment 
policy is gender-neutral and demographic-neutral. Most of our facilities undergo social compliance audits from 
customers, third party and are certified under SA 8000 standards, where gender neutrality is an important part of 
social compliance.
Our DEI approach is supported by governance mechanisms, policies, awareness programmes and inclusive hiring 
practices. Sustainability reporting, reviewed at the Board level, includes social compliance, human rights records, 
fair wages, working conditions and disciplinary management, alongside broader ESG priorities.
Our DEI goals
 Foster a diverse 
workforce that reflects the 
communities we serve
 Create an inclusive culture 
that values and respects 
individual differences
 Ensure equal 
opportunities for growth 
and development
 Attract, retain and develop 
diverse talent
Organisation-wide DEI 
communication
Communication of DEI goals 
and initiatives remains central 
to building an inclusive and 
respectful workplace. We use 
internal communication channels, 
the IHRMS employee portal, 
company newsletters, workshops 
and leadership engagement forums 
to communicate our DEI agenda. 
A dedicated ESG Board provides 
strategic insight on DEI initiatives.
Training programmes on POSH, 
DEI, unconscious bias, human 
rights, business ethics and values 
continue to build awareness 
and accountability across 
the organisation.
Institutionalising DEI through 
policies and programmes
We remain committed to building 
a workplace where employees 
are treated fairly and are able to

based environment. Our Human

Assessment and Development 
Centre
The Assessment and Development 
Centre plays a key role in building 
technical and leadership pipelines 
from line leadership to mid-
management. It supports internal 
talent mobility by enabling 
structured movement of employees 
across roles and functions, 
while offering clearer career 
progression pathways.
The ADC follows a competency-
based assessment approach, 
ensuring that promotion and 
development decisions are 
objective, transparent and aligned 
with leadership and capability 
requirements. It uses a combination 
of AI-based evaluation tools and a 
hybrid assessor framework, where 
AI acts as an enabler to supplement 
assessment by qualified assessors. 
This strengthens neutrality, consistency and benchmarking 
against industry standards.
Candidates are evaluated 
across functional capability, 
leadership competencies, 
behavioural attributes, learning 
agility and readiness for higher 
responsibilities. The methodology 
includes situational judgement 
tests, in-basket exercises, role plays 
and case studies to assess potential 
and readiness.
The insights generated through 
the ADC support the creation of 
Individual Development Plans, 
enabling targeted training, role 
rotations and upskilling. This 
structured approach helps identify 
high-potential talent, supports 
competency-based promotions 
and builds a more predictable 
succession pipeline for critical mid-
management roles.During FY26, ADC coverage 
increased by approximately 
32.5% compared to the 
previous year. Around 91% of 
the 135 employees promoted

retained, reflecting the impact 
of structured development and 
career progression pathways.EMPLOYEE ENGAGEMENT

SOCIAL COMPLIANCE
Aurobindo Pharma’s human rights, 
ethics and social compliance 
framework is built on international 
standards, responsible workplace 
practices and structured grievance 
redressal. During FY26, the focus 
remained on strengthening 
implementation, monitoring 
and awareness.
Formulation units are covered 
under SA 8000:2014 standards, 
covering social compliance, 
labour standards, health, safety 
and environmental aspects. 
The formulation division also 
achieved RSPO certification, 
supporting responsible sourcing 
and environmental preservation. 
Oral dosage and injectable units 
are also covered under the SMETA 
audit framework, supporting ethical 
trade, labour standards and ESG-
linked compliance.
Two of the manufacturing facilities 
(APL Unit VII and APL Unit HC I) are 
certified for SA8000:2014.Human rights framework
Our human rights framework 
aligns with ILO conventions and 
global human rights norms. It 
covers prohibition of child and 
forced labour, non-discrimination, 
equal opportunity, fair wages, 
safe working conditions, 
freedom of association and 
collective bargaining.
HR teams across the value chain 
remain responsible for periodic 
monitoring and implementation of 
these standards.
Grievance redressal mechanism
Employees can raise complaints 
and suggestions through People 
Care Link in HRMS by dialling the 
hotline number 77666 or sending a 
dedicated email to humanrights@
aurobindo.com
The Human Rights Compliance 
Hotline enables confidential 
and anonymous reporting 
for employees, vendors and 
other stakeholders.
Each unit has a Grievance 
Redressal Committee to ensure 
timely investigation, confidential 
handling and protection against 
retaliation. The mechanism is 
supported by the Code of Conduct, 
whistleblower systems and 
ethics frameworks.
Due diligence and audits
Human rights and ethics 
compliance are reviewed annually 
by Corporate HR and Senior 
Management. Manufacturing 
and R&D units are assessed 
on child labour, forced labour, 
discrimination, harassment, wages 
and working conditions.
All units undergo statutory and 
third-party audits. In the supply 
chain, 100% of critical suppliers are 
screened for human rights risks, 
and around 70% of key suppliers 
are assessed under the Supplier 
Code of Conduct.
No significant human rights or 
ethical violations were reported 
during the year.Dr. Suresh received HCA 2025 GOLD award from The Economic Times.

OCCUPATIONAL HEALTH AND 
SAFETY 
The health and safety of our 
people is non-negotiable and 
fundamental to our operational 
integrity. We are committed to 
providing a safe and healthy 
workplace for all stakeholders 
Policy and governance
Occupational health and safety 
remains a key material priority 
for Aurobindo Pharma. We 
are committed to providing a 
safe, healthy and responsible 
work environment across 
our manufacturing facilities, 
R&D centres, subsidiaries and 
support functions.
Our approach is guided by the 
Environment, Health, Safety and 
Sustainability (EHS&S) policy, 
which applies to employees, 
contractors, subcontractors, visitors 
and neighbouring communities. 
We also encourage suppliers and 
vendors to follow safe, healthy 
and environmentally responsible 
practices aligned with our Supplier 
Code of Conduct.
Health and safety systems are 
implemented across all plants and 
are supported by corporate policies, 
procedures, site-level controls and 
continuous improvement initiatives. 
Safety performance is overseen by 
the Central Safety Committee (CSC), 
comprising senior management through globally benchmarked 
policies, robust processes, 
proactive hazard management, and 
continuous training. We believe 
that achieving strong health and 
safety performance requires 
both organisational commitment 
and individual responsibility. By fostering a culture where 
everyone takes ownership of 
safety, we continue to strengthen 
our safety performance and drive 
continuous improvement across 
our operations.
Risk Management and Emergency Preparedness Plan Governance
•  Policies and Procedures on 
Environment, Health, Safety 
and Sustainability
• Health and safety systems
• Central Safety Committee
     for oversight

Identifying and addressing 
potential hazards
We follow a structured approach 
to identifying, evaluating and 
mitigating occupational health and 
safety risks. A corporate guidance 
document supports teams in 
assessing risks and reducing 
them to acceptable levels through 
strengthened controls or additional 
preventive measures.
Work-related hazards are identified 
through design checklists, Hazard 
and Operability Analysis (HAZOP), 
Hazard Identification and Risk 
Assessment (HIRA), Job safety 
analysis (JSA) and activity-based 
risk assessments for both routine 
and non-routine activities, as well 
as qualitative and quantitative risk 
assessments. These assessments 
help minimise hazards and take appropriate preventive measures. 
These are supported by EHS 
trainings, internal health and safety 
audits, inspections and site-level 
reviews conducted in line with 
corporate guidelines.
Gemba walks are conducted to 
observe work practices, interact 
with shopfloor teams and identify 
health and safety risks through 
direct engagement. Toolbox talks 
are conducted in all sites which 
further support daily health 
and safety communication, 
while corrective and preventive 
actions are taken wherever gaps 
are identified. Workmen are 
encouraged in these forums by 
sharing suggestions and feedback 
for improvement.
We also conduct periodic inter-unit 
audits for gap assessment and 
performance improvement, along 
with knowledge-sharing sessions 
to communicate best safety 
practices across manufacturing 
facilities. The third-party health and 
safety audits are also conducted by 
the competent authorities approved •  Gemba walks for frontline

Certification status
16 of our manufacturing facilities 
are ISO 14001:2015 certified, one 
is ISO 45001:2018 certified, and 
two are SA 8000:2014 certified. 
Certifications for other facilities are 
in progress.
Other Environment, Health and 
Safety training: This covers 
broad topics like handling of 
hazardous chemicals, spill 
control, work permit system, 
emergency measures like 
OSEP , communication of near 
miss and incidents, specific 
training to ERT members on 
emergency preparedness and 
response, behaviour-based 
safety, ergonomics training, 
usage of personal protective 
equipment (PPE), hazardous 
waste management, conservation 
of water, wastewater treatment 
and reuse, implementation of 
environmental management 
systems (ISO 14001 
requirements), etc.
OHS trainings are mandatory 
and generally achieve full 
coverage. These programmes help 
employees and contract workmen 
understand workplace hazards, 
safety protocols, procedures 
and guidelines. At the beginning 
of each year, individual training 
needs are identified and used 
to prepare a training calendar covering key OHS awareness 
topics. Periodic refresher sessions 
and Lean Daily Management 
meetings with senior leadership 
further support action tracking and 
continuous improvement.
Open Communication
We encourage open dialogue 
on safety and provide channels 
for employees and contract 
workmen to report hazards, unsafe 
conditions and improvement 
suggestions without fear of 
reprisal. This helps strengthen early 
risk identification and supports a 
more transparent safety culture.
Recognition and Rewards
We have established systems to 
recognise employees and contract 
workmen who demonstrate safe 
behaviour, contribute improvement 
ideas and support compliance 
with safety practices. Safety Week 
celebrations are conducted across 
locations, with participation in 
quizzes, poster-making, safety 
skits and safety improvement 
demonstrations. These initiatives 
help build awareness while by the regulatory bodies to 
further evaluate the gaps and take 
necessary actions / improvements. 
Each manufacturing facility uses 
an EHS scorecard to monitor key 
safety indicators on a monthly 
basis, enabling regular tracking and 
improvement of safety systems.
Product and process safety
Product and process safety is 
an important part of our EHS 
framework. Risk identification and 
assessment are undertaken before 
process scale-up, enabling teams 
to identify potential hazards and 
establish suitable controls.
Before any chemical process is 
initiated in the manufacturing area, 
HAZOP studies are conducted. 
These are supported by qualitative 
and quantitative risk assessments 
to help ensure that appropriate 
safeguards are in place. Periodic 
reviews are undertaken to assess 
the effectiveness of existing 
systems and identify opportunities 
for further improvement in health 
and safety performance.
EMERGENCY PREPAREDNESS 
AND RESPONSE
All our manufacturing and R&D 
facilities have on-site emergency 
preparedness plans covering 
credible emergency scenarios, 
including fire and chemical spill 
incidents. These plans are reviewed 
periodically and supported by 
periodic mock drills including site 
evacuation which are conducted on 
all identified potential emergency  
scenarios like fire, chemical 
leakages/spillages etc., at each 
facility in compliance with the 
statutory requirement.
Each location has a trained 
Emergency Response Team 
(ERT), first aiders and an incident 
management team equipped to 
respond to emergencies across all 
shifts. The ERT details are displayed 
at prominent places in the site 
to communicate and co-ordinate 
easily during emergencies. In addition, an Emergency Control 
Centre (ECC) equipped with 
necessary emergency equipment 
and an Occupational Health 
Centre (OHC) is made available for 
immediate response and support. 
We also maintain mutual aid 
arrangements with neighbouring 
industries and local government 
fire stations as an additional line 
of defence.
Our sites are equipped with first 
aid kits and emergency equipment 
beyond statutory requirements. 
We have also established Onsite 
Emergency Preparedness Plans 
(OSEP), standard operating 
procedures, operational control 
procedures and work instructions 
to ensure employees and contract 
workmen are trained to respond 
effectively to emergencies and 
workplace hazards.
Training is conducted through 
shopfloor sessions, classroom 
programmes and practical 
training sessions.
PROMOTING A CULTURE OF 
SAFETY
We continue to strengthen a 
workplace culture where safety is 
owned collectively by employees, 
contractors and site leadership. During FY26, safety awareness 
initiatives and behavioural 
interventions were conducted 
across locations to improve risk 
perception, reinforce safe work 
practices and encourage proactive 
participation in identifying and 
addressing potential hazards.
Training and Development
We provide comprehensive 
training on occupational health 
and safety, specific work-related 
hazards, hazardous activities and 
situations to all our employees, 
including permanent workers and 
contractors. We have implemented 
well-designed programmes 
towards this, including:
Job-specific training:  This training 
delves into the specific hazards 
and safety protocols relevant to 
different job roles, such as safe 
storage, handling of hazardous 
chemicals, safe operation 
of equipment like reactors, 
centrifuges, dryers, and change 
control procedures.
Regulatory compliance training: 
This training covers specific safety 
regulations mandated by law and 
helps ensure compliance and 
protect workers.recognising individuals and 
teams that contribute to improved 
safety performance.
ENCOURAGING INCIDENT 
REPORTING AND 
INVESTIGATION
We encourage timely reporting of 
incidents, near misses and unsafe 
conditions to strengthen preventive 
action and improve learning 
across sites. Incident reporting 
and investigation processes are 
supported by defined escalation 
channels, root cause analysis 
and corrective and preventive 
action tracking.
Non-compliances and safety 
observations, where identified, are 
reviewed and addressed through 
corrective and preventive action 
plans with defined timelines and 
follow-up verification. Independent 
SMETA audits, internal audits, 
HR audits and functional reviews 
further support compliance 
monitoring across employee and 
contractor workforces.

ENERGY TRANSITION
We continue to advance towards 
carbon-neutral growth, integrating 
decarbonisation into operational 
and strategic decision-making. Our 
roadmap remains aligned with the 
Science Based Targets initiative 
(SBTi), supporting global efforts to 
limit temperature rise in line with 
the Paris Agreement.
During the year, emissions were 
influenced by the addition and 
ramp-up of newer facilities, 
including Lyfius, Aurovitas 
China and Qule. As these sites 
progress towards optimal capacity 
utilisation, the focus remains on 
improving operating efficiency, 
stabilising resource consumption 
and embedding energy 
management practices from the 
early stages of scale-up.
Transitioning to renewable 
energy
Renewable energy adoption 
remains a key lever in reducing 
operational emissions. During the 
year, we consumed 1,70,250 MWh of renewable power, representing 
approximately 18.4% of our total 
electricity requirement.
This includes a mix of captive 
generation, rooftop solar 
installations and power 
procurement through strategic 
partnerships. During the year, 
Eugia Steriles commissioned a 1 MW rooftop solar plant, while 
we also entered into a power 
purchase agreement with Garuda 
Renewables to source hybrid wind 
and solar energy. These initiatives 
expand renewable sourcing across 
facilities and strengthen long-term 
energy security. Also Aurobindo 
Pharma acquired 26% stake in 
Swarnaakshu Solar Power.

We continued the transition 
from conventional fuels such 
as coal and furnace oil towards 
cleaner alternatives. Biomass-
based fuels and natural gas are 
increasingly being adopted across 
manufacturing facilities.
In FY26, 5,53,567 GJ of energy 
was generated from biomass, 
accounting for approximately 
~5.8% of total energy 
consumption, while 1,63,242 
GJ was generated from natural 
gas. This shift contributes to 
emissions reduction while 
improving fuel efficiency and 
operational flexibility.
Optimising energy efficiency
Energy efficiency remains a 
core focus area, driven through 
continuous monitoring, process 
optimisation and technology 
upgrades. Dedicated teams assess energy and steam 
consumption across facilities 
and implement technologically 
advanced solutions to 
optimise efficiency and lower 
resource usage.
Regular energy audits help 
identify improvement areas and 
guide targeted interventions 
across high-energy-consuming 
equipment, utilities and 
processes. Key initiatives 
include equipment optimisation, 
reduction of heat losses, recovery 
of steam condensate and process-
level efficiency improvements. 
These measures continue to 
deliver sustained energy savings 
and support emissions reduction 
across operations.
Managing Scope 3 emissions
We are progressively 
strengthening our approach 
to value chain emissions. During FY26, we undertook a 
comprehensive Scope 3 inventory 
across relevant upstream and 
downstream categories, in line with 
the GHG Protocol.
Logistics optimisation remains an 
important lever. A significant share 
of exports continues to be routed 
through sea transport, with >90% 
of shipments moving through this 
lower-emission mode. We also 
work with logistics providers to 
maintain emissions dashboards 
aligned with the GHG Accounting 
Protocol, helping improve visibility 
and tracking across our distribution 
network. We aim to sustain 
and further enhance sea-route 
movement to >90% of exports.
For Scope 3 emissions calculation, 
we considered 8 relevant 
categories under the GHG Protocol. 
Going forward, our focus areas 
include upstream logistics, sold 
products, investments.

AIR POLLUTION CONTROL 
MEASURES
Air emissions at our facilities 
mainly originate from boilers, DG 
sets, and process fugitive sources, 
which are continuously monitored 
through Online Continuous 
Monitoring System (OCMS) 
also. Third-party monitoring is 
also conducted for ambient air 
and stack emission monitoring, 
ensuring compliance with 
regulatory limits. Flue gases from 
coal-fired boilers are channelled 
through multi-cyclones, bag filters 
and Electrostatic Precipitators 
(ESP) to control particulate 
emissions as applicable and as 
prescribed by statutory authorities. 
Monthly stack emission 
reports confirm adherence to 
specified limits.
Key Emission Control Facilities:
  Boilers: Equipped with multi-
cyclones, bag filters and 
ESPs to control particulate 
emissions as applicable.
  Continuous Emission 
Monitoring Systems: 
Installed to track VOCs, 
PM, SOx, NOx, and treated 
wastewater parameters 
(TDS, COD, etc.), with real-
time data shared with the 
State Pollution Control Board 
(SPCB) as applicable for 
compliance monitoring. Ambient Air Quality (AAQ) 
Monitoring Stations: AAQ  
stations are installed to 
SPCB and Central Pollution 
Control Board (CPCB) servers 
for compliance monitoring 
and reporting.
 DG Sets: Fitted with acoustic 
enclosures to control 
noise pollution.
 Solvent Storage & Handling: 
Vent condensers are installed 
to minimise evaporation 
losses and fugitive 
emissions. Solvent transfer is 
carried through closed loop 
system to further reduce 
fugitive emissions.
 Scrubbers: Installed 
to control acid/alkali 
emissions from reactors and 
storage tanks.
 HTDS Effluent Storage Tanks: 
Equipped with hoods and 
scrubbers to control volatile 
organic compounds (VOCs).
 Online Monitoring Systems: 
Track high and low TDS 
effluent streams, with 
data shared directly with 
State and Central Pollution 
Control Board (SPCB, CPCB) 
servers. RO permeate is also 
monitored and reported to 
regulatory authorities.GHG Emission Reduction 
Strategies
Combined Heat and Power 
(CHP) plants constitute a critical 
component of high-efficiency 
energy systems deployed across 
the group, two in Apitoria 
facilities, one in Eugia and one in 
Lyfius, specifically engineered to 
minimise greenhouse gas (GHG) 
emissions through a “steam-first” 
operational philosophy.
Within this optimised configuration, 
the generation of steam is 
established as the primary 
performance objective, while the 
concurrent generation of electrical 
power is realised as an inherent 
co-product, effectively translating 
into measurable utility cost savings 
and energy optimisation. By 
systematically capturing, recovering, 
and reutilising thermal energy that 
would otherwise be dissipated as 
waste heat in conventional power 
generation cycles, CHP systems 
significantly enhance overall energy 
conversion efficiency and reduce 
specific fuel consumption.
For the pharmaceutical 
manufacturing units, the 
implementation of an integrated 
energy model delivers a substantial 
dual benefit: it consistently meets 
the intensive and quality-critical 
steam requirements of regulated 
production processes, while 
=== page 75 ===

simultaneously enabling on-site 
power generation. This integrated 
approach results in a reduced 
dependence on external grid 
electricity, lowers the baseline 
carbon intensity of operations, 
and strengthens alignment with 
defined ESG commitments, 
decarbonisation pathways, and 
sustainability performance targets.
Pharmaceutical manufacturing faces 
the dual challenge of achieving 
Green House Gas (GHG) reduction 
targets while ensuring uninterrupted 
power supply for process-critical 
operations. To address this, one of 
the Eugia facility (Eugia II – Bhiwadi, 
Rajasthan) has implemented a 
resilient and low-emission energy 
architecture integrating dual-fuel 
and gas-based generation systems. 
Dual fuel gensets provide flexibility 
to operate on gaseous fuel, 
ensuring reliability while optimising 
combustion efficiency and reducing 
emission intensity. In parallel, 
three-Megawatt (MW) class natural 
gas-based generator sets, offering 
cleaner combustion compared to 
conventional diesel systems. This integrated approach reduces GHG 
emissions, while contributing to 
a reduction in the facility’s carbon 
footprint, thereby reinforcing its 
commitment to sustainable and 
resilient operations.
Environment Training programs
Aurobindo has a system of 
conducting periodic training 
programs which is an integral 
part of Environmental 
Management System (ISO 14001) 
implementation across all the 
manufacturing facilities, including 
ESG aspects to bring awareness on 
the compliance needs, emerging 
industry requirements and 
regulatory aspects. 
The trainings focus on:
1.  Energy Conservation
  This program equips teams 
with practical strategies to 
optimise energy efficiency, 
focusing on steam system 
management, condensate 
recovery, and insulation 
to minimise heat loss. 
Participants learn to operate and maintain utility systems 
like boilers, refrigeration 
units, and electrical 
distribution networks for 
peak performance. Hands-
on workshops cover energy 
audits, automation controls, 
energy use optimisation in 
process to drive measurable 
savings. The goal is to reduce 
carbon emissions and 
operational impacts while 
ensuring compliance. 
2.   Water Conservation & 
Wastewater Reuse Training
  Designed for facility teams, 
this program enables adoption 
of water-saving techniques 
such as water conservation, 
leak detection, and closed-loop 
recycling. Participants also 
gain expertise in advanced 
wastewater treatment 
methods, including membrane 
bioreactors (MBRs) and 
zero liquid discharge (ZLD) 
systems, which are in place to 
meet regulatory requirements. 
Training includes water 
Training on Energy Conservation
non-hazardous waste, in 
compliance with local and 
international regulations. 
Participants learn to identify 
waste streams, chemical 
safety, use of appropriate 
PPE, and follow emergency 
response protocols for 
spill prevention. The 
training also covers reuse, 
recycling, and responsible 
disposal of electronic and 
plastic materials, Extended 
Producer Responsibility 
(EPR) compliance, and best 
practices for minimising 
environmental impact. 
By embedding these 
principles, we ensure 
regulatory compliance and 
operational safety. 
 ESG trainings were 
provided to cross-functional 
departments in India 
and abroad regarding 
national and international 
reporting requirements 
as per global frameworks 
across Energy, Emissions, 
Water Management, Waste Management in Environment, 
Employee wellbeing and

in social aspects and key 
governance aspects at 
group level.
 Sustainability efforts extend 
to key functions, such as

teams work with suppliers to 
reduce environmental impact 
to comply with customer 
requirements and regulations, 
and promote the use of eco-
friendly materials. 
 To ensure effectiveness, 
trainings are delivered 
through diverse formats 
such as classroom sessions,

regularly updated to align 
with evolving regulations. 
The effectiveness is measured 
through assessments and 
feedback which ensures

  It also includes focused

on Pharmaceuticals in

3.   Raw Material Optimisation 
& Process Efficiency Training
 This program empowers 
production teams to reduce

Participants learn to optimise

also covers sustainable

Water remains a critical resource 
across our manufacturing 
processes. Our approach 
focuses on reducing freshwater 
dependency through efficiency, 
reuse and recycling, while 
ensuring compliance with 
regulatory standards.
We continue to optimise water 
consumption through process 
improvements, real-time 
monitoring and regular audits. 
Key initiatives include recovery 
and reuse of steam condensate, 
optimisation of water usage in 
utilities, and reuse of rejected water 
streams across operations.
Wastewater treatment, reuse 
and recycling
We adopt a proactive and 
holistic approach to wastewater 
management, ensuring compliance 
with pollution prevention and 
control standards across our 
operations. The manufacturing 
units operate with advanced 
effluent treatment systems designed for effective collection, 
treatment and disposal 
of wastewater.
Select facilities have achieved 
zero liquid discharge (ZLD) status, 
while non-ZLD units undertake 
primary treatment before sending 
wastewater to Common Effluent 
Treatment Plants (CETPs), in line 
with applicable regulatory norms.
Recycling and reuse of treated 
wastewater remain central to 
reducing freshwater intake and 
improving overall water efficiency.
Rainwater harvesting
Rainwater harvesting continues to 
support groundwater recharge and 
reduce dependency on external 
sources. Our efforts include 
installing harvesting pits within 
premises and even undertaking 
rainwater conservation outside the 
facilities, where possible. During 
FY26, we harvested 1,77,732 KL 
of rainwater across facilities, 
contributing to long-term water 
security for both operations and 
surrounding communities.Our water performance in FY26

WASTE MANAGEMENT AND 
CIRCULARITY
Our waste management 
approach is anchored in 
minimising waste generation at 
source and ensuring responsible 
handling across its lifecycle.
Waste segregation at source 
enables efficient recycling, 
co-processing and disposal. 
Hazardous waste is primarily 
directed towards co-processing, 
while non-hazardous waste 
streams, including plastics, are 
managed through recycling 
and Extended Producer 
Responsibility (EPR) frameworks.
However, the Company continues 
to maintain high levels of co-
processing and recycling, with 
a sustained focus on reducing 
landfill disposal and improving 
circularity outcomes.

ADDRESSING ANTIMICROBIAL 
RESISTANCE (AMR)
As a pharmaceutical manufacturer, 
addressing antimicrobial resistance 
remains a critical responsibility. 
Our approach is aligned with 
global frameworks and industry 
best practices.
We monitor antibiotic 
concentrations in treated 
wastewater in accordance with 
Predicted No-Effect Concentration 
(PNEC) thresholds defined by the 
AMR Industry Alliance. All relevant 
manufacturing facilities operate 
within these limits, supported 
by robust monitoring and 
validation mechanisms.
During the year, we continued 
participation in the AMR Benchmark 2026, led by the 
Access to Medicine Foundation, 
an independent organisation that 
assesses how pharmaceutical 
companies support access to 
medicines and respond to global 
health priorities such as AMR.
We also remain an active 
member of the AMR Industry 
Alliance, contributing to collective 
efforts focused on responsible 
manufacturing, improved access 
and reduced environmental 
impact. Our processes incorporate 
established deactivation methods 
for antibiotic residues and follow 
globally recognised methodologies, 
including the mass balance 
approach recommended by WHO 
and AMR frameworks.To support transparent 
assessment, we also collaborate 
with international agencies by 
providing access for the collection 
and analysis of treated wastewater 
samples, helping validate antibiotic 
content and strengthen confidence 
in our environmental controls.BIODIVERSITY AND 
ECOSYSTEM CONSERVATION
We continue to strengthen 
biodiversity conservation through 
structured greenbelt development 
and ecosystem-focused initiatives. 
A dedicated eco-development 
wing within our Environment, 
Health and Safety (EHS) team leads 
high-impact initiatives and drives 
progress against defined goals.
Our greenbelt footprint spans 
approximately 837 hectares, with 
over 4,65,633 trees planted across 
operational and surrounding areas. 
These plantations comprise native 
and climate-resilient species, 
supporting ecological balance and 
soil health. 
Sustained maintenance practices 
and efficient irrigation systems 
enable survival rates exceeding 
80%, ensuring long-term ecological 
impact. These efforts also 
contribute to carbon sequestration 
and improved environmental 
quality around our facilities. In 
FY26, these efforts helped avoid

RESPONSIBLE SUPPLY CHAIN
We continue to embed 
sustainability across our supply 
chain through structured 
assessments, supplier 
engagement and robust 
governance practices.
Approximately 70% of key 
starting material suppliers are 
assessed on ESG parameters 
under our Supplier Code of 
Conduct. The framework extends 
beyond quality and compliance 
to cover environmental 
performance, labour practices, 
ethics, health and safety, and 
management systems.As a full member of the 
Pharmaceutical Supply Chain 
Initiative (PSCI), we align our 
supplier practices with global 
standards for responsible supply 
chain management. Suppliers 
are evaluated through audits, 
ongoing monitoring and social 
compliance assessments aligned 
with frameworks such as SMETA 
and SA 8000.
Through continued engagement 
and knowledge-sharing initiatives, 
we aim to strengthen transparency, 
resilience and sustainability across 
our supplier ecosystem.
Local sourcing
We prioritise sourcing from 
local suppliers that demonstrate 
sound environmental and social 
practices. This supports local 
economies, promotes responsible 
manufacturing and helps reduce 
transportation-related emissions.
Where possible, we engage 
suppliers located close to our 
production facilities to improve 
supply chain efficiency, reduce 
logistical complexity and lower 
associated carbon emissions. 
All such suppliers are evaluated 
against our compliance, quality and 
sustainability expectations.
